public_payload.normalized_proposition: Claimed AI breakthroughs rarely prove general enough to live up to initial expectations, often working only in some contexts.

statement.excerpt: But “breakthroughs” rarely turn to be general to live up to initial rosy expectations. Often advances work in some contexts, not otherwise.

from_speaker: live up to initial rosy expectations
Often advances work in some contexts, not otherwise.
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is a historical frequency claim about publicly touted AI advances before the post.
Generality should be assessed against the initial expectations for each advance, not against an added requirement that every advance achieve general intelligence.
The retrospective period ends on the post date. The source supplies no starting date, population of breakthroughs, or numerical meaning for rarely.
criteria.support_condition: A reasonably representative historical comparison finds that meeting initially expected generality was uncommon and failures across contexts were common.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable historical comparison finds that advances commonly met their initial expectations for generality.
